RF-SCGFS: A Feature Selection Method Based on Secuer and Random Forest Model for Single-cell RNA-Seq Data
candidates.abstract:
Introduction:
                    Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is crucial for unraveling gene
expression complexity. However, existing feature selection methods often overlook the biological
significance of co-expressed gene regions, leading to the omission of potential biomarkers.
                  
                  
                    Methods:
                    We propose RF-SCGFS, a co-expressed gene region and gene joint selection method
based on random forests. The method identifies co-expressed gene regions within homologous cell
populations and builds a random forest model using cell type labels generated by the Scalable and
Efficient speCtral clUstERing algorithm (Secuer). Feature importance evaluation is applied to select
key co-expressed gene regions and genes.
                  
                  
                    Results:
                    Experiments on 13 public scRNA-seq datasets demonstrate that RF-SCGFS outperforms
traditional methods with average improvements of 0.15 and 0.19 in normalized mutual information
(NMI) and adjusted Rand index (ARI), respectively. When combined with mainstream unsupervised
algorithms, RF-SCGFS achieves excellent performance (NMI > 0.91 on Yan and Biase datasets). In
the PBMC-ctrl dataset, the method successfully identifies genes associated with immune system processes
(GO:0006955, p = 2.02E-37).
                  
                  
                    Discussion:
                    RF-SCGFS addresses key challenges in single-cell analysis by reducing computational
burden through efficient feature selection while maintaining biological relevance through unsupervised
clustering-guided selection.
                  
                  
                    Conclusion:
                    RF-SCGFS provides an interpretable framework for feature selection in single-cell data,
successfully identifying relevant disease genes and revealing the potential value of co-expressed
gene regions in analyzing cellular heterogeneity.

MO03.1.A Spike-in probe-enhanced single-cell RNA-seq reveals post-infusion transcriptomic remodeling of “prime-and-kill” synNotch-CAR-T cells
candidates.abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Background
                    We previously developed synthetic Notch (synNotch)-chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells to improve the safety and efficacy of CAR-T therapy for glioblastoma. In this system, an anti-EphA2/IL13Rα2-dual-CAR is expressed only upon recognition of tumor- or brain-specific “priming” antigens, EGFRvIII (termed E-SYNC cells) or brevican (B-SYNC), respectively, with E-SYNC currently under phase I clinical evaluation (NCT06186401). However, tracking and profiling these engineered cells in vivo remain challenging, limiting our understanding of their activity and therapeutic potential. To address this gap, we developed a single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) workflow with custom spike-in probes targeting synNotch-CAR transcripts, enabling simultaneous detection of engineered cells and transcriptomic profiling.
                  
                  
                    Material and Methods
                    Using the 10X Genomics Flex Gene Expression platform, we incorporated 20 custom spike-in probes into a premanufactured whole-transcriptome probe set to detect synNotch-CAR transcripts. This workflow was evaluated in vitro using E-SYNC and B-SYNC cells and in vivo using xenograft models treated with a single intravenous infusion of B-SYNC cells. We assessed detection of synNotch-positive cells and performed single-cell transcriptomic profiling to characterize post-infusion dynamics, including tissue-specific and antigen-dependent changes.
                  
                  
                    Results
                    In vitro, integration of multiple probes using machine-learning-assisted classifiers detected 78.2% of E-SYNC cells and 60.0% of B-SYNC cells with 98.0% specificity. In xenograft models, synNotch-positive cells were detected across spleen, lung, and brain tissues, with the highest frequency and most robust priming and activation observed in the brain. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses revealed tissue-specific differentiation programs, including cytotoxicity, proliferation, metabolic activity, and acquisition of tissue-resident memory phenotypes, shaped by both environmental cues and synNotch-mediated antigen recognition.
                  
                  
                    Conclusion
                    This spike-in probe-enhanced scRNA-seq workflow enables robust detection and high-resolution characterization of synNotch-CAR-T cell dynamics, providing a broadly applicable platform for monitoring engineered immune cells across diverse clinical contexts.

Benchmarking computational tools for locus-specific analysis of transposable elements in single-cell RNA-seq datasets
candidates.abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Background
                    Transposable elements (TEs) are increasingly recognized as regulators of gene expression and cellular identity. Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables the analysis of their transcription at cellular resolution, but the repetitive nature of TEs and their frequent overlap with genes create substantial mapping ambiguity. Although several tools quantify TE expression, few support locus-specific analysis, and their performance in single-cell data has not been systematically evaluated.
                  
                  
                    Results
                    We present a comprehensive, scalable benchmarking framework written in Snakemake for locus-level TE quantification in short-read scRNA-seq data, combining real datasets with simulations that provide read-level ground truth. Our simulations show that sequence-diverged insertions can be quantified with relatively high accuracy, whereas young TEs remain difficult to resolve due to unreliable assignment of multi-mapping reads. We observe pronounced family-specific biases and identify gene-TE disambiguation as a major unresolved challenge. Across the evaluated methods, incorporating multi-mapping reads generally increased false-positive calls without substantially improving locus-level accuracy. When loci of all ages were analyzed together, SoloTE in unique-mapper mode achieved the highest detection accuracy.
                  
                  
                    Conclusions
                    Our benchmark delineates the fundamental limits imposed by short-read scRNA-seq on locus-specific TE quantification, providing practical guidance for prospective users. Suggested best practices include focusing locus-level analyses on older insertions, applying unique-mapper strategies to improve precision, aggregating counts at the subfamily level for young TEs, and explicitly checking for gene-TE overlaps. Our workflow is reproducible and extensible, providing a foundation for evaluating emerging methods aimed at resolving TE transcription at single-locus resolution.

candidates.title: Development of immunogenic cell death-related biomarkers for the diagnosis of ischemic stroke based on transcriptomic microarray and single-cell RNA-seq
candidates.abstract:
Background
                    This study investigated the role of immunogenic cell death (ICD) in ischemic stroke (IS) by integrating human peripheral-blood microarray transcriptomic biomarker discovery with mouse brain single-cell analysis of cellular heterogeneity
                  
                  
                    Methods
                    Biological functions related to the biomarkers were assessed through enrichment and immune-infiltration analyses. Candidate compounds were prioritized using Graph-Based Attention Network (GraphBAN) prediction followed by molecular docking. The mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) scRNA-seq dataset GSE174574 was further interrogated to map biomarker expression and transcription factor (TF) activity in key cells. Biomarker expression was experimentally examined in CoCl₂-induced hypoxic microglial cells using RT-qPCR.hypoxic microglial cells using reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR).
                  
                  
                    Results
                    The analysis defined TLR2, TNFSF10, and RALBP1 as immunogenic cell death-related biomarkers in IS, with patient-level validation in the baseline subset of GSE58294. Pathway results connected these genes with inflammatory response, TNFA signaling via NFKB, interferon alpha response, and IL6-JAK-STAT3 signaling. TLR2 was positively associated with neutrophils and monocytes, whereas TNFSF10TLR2 was positively associated with neutrophils, whereas TNFSF10 showed a negative relationship with B cells. Docking analysis supported favorable interactions of the biomarkers with tert-butyl 2-thiocyanatoacetate. Docking analysis predicted binding energies ranging from −4.9 to −9.6 kcal/mol for the candidate compounds against the three biomarkers. In the single-cell trajectory, expression of all three biomarkers shifted markedly during microglial differentiation. CoCl₂-induced hypoxia also increased TLR2, RALBP1, and TNFSF10 expression in microglial cells. Atf4, Hif1a, Fosl2, and related TFs were more active in ISMCAO samples.
                  
                  
                    Conclusion
                    TLR2, TNFSF10, and RALBP1 may serve as immunogenic cell death-related biomarkers for IS. These results offer a molecular foundation for future development of precision-targeted therapeutic strategies in IS.

Effect of sourdough fermentation on the physical properties and sensory characteristics of bread made from Wheat (Triticum aestivum), Orange-Fleshed Sweet Potato (Ipomoea batata L.) and Soybean (Glycine max L.) Composite Flour
candidates.journal: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF FOOD SCIENCE AND QUALITY CONTROL
candidates.abstract:
Sourdough bread was prepared by fermentation of wheat flour, orange-fleshed sweet potato and
soybean composite flour using strains of Lactobacillus plantarum and Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
To evaluate the effect of sourdough fermentation on the physical properties and sensory
characteristics of the sourdough bread, the product was analyzed for loaf weight, height, volume,
texture; crack and crust colour then subjected to sensory evaluation. The results revealed that the
sourdough loaf weight, height and volume were; 153.2g, 1.88cm and 218cm3
, while the control
sample was 181.1g, 1.26cm and 216cm3
, respectively. There was no significant (p>0.05)
difference in texture, crack and crust colour. Sensory characteristics showed appearance (6.75
and 6.0), taste (6.45 and 5.83), aroma (5.66 and 4.75), texture (6.44 and 5.33) and overall
acceptability (6.33 and 5.25) of sourdough bread and the control sample respectively.
Fermentation positively had impact on the physical properties and sensory characteristics of
sourdough bread produced. Lactic acid bacteria strains have the ability to improve loaf weight,
height, volume and sensory acceptability. Sourdough fermentation technology is recommended to
improve dough quality without adding baker’s yeast.

candidates.title: Quality Evaluation of Sourdough Bread Produced Using Wheat (Triticum aestivum), Orange-Fleshed Sweet Potato (Ipomoea batata L.) and Soybean (Glycine max L.) Composite Flour
candidates.journal: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF FOOD SCIENCE AND QUALITY CONTROL
candidates.abstract:
Sourdough bread fermented with Lactobacillus plantarum, Lactobacillus brevis and
Saccharomyces cerevisiae was produced from a combination of three flours (wheat, orange flesh
potato and soybean). The flour used in the investigation was assessed for functional and proximate
composition while the sourdough bread produced was evaluated for nutritional composition,
physical properties and glycemic index. Bread leavened with commercial yeast (Saccharomyces
cerevisiae) served as control. The flour samples possessed good functional and proximate
properties. Bulk density, water/oil absorption capacity and swelling index ranged from 0.54 – 0.77
g/cm3, 2.42-3.79%, 1.32-1.42% and 1.36-2.44%, respectively, for wheat, orange flesh potato and
soybean. Moisture content varied from 4.48 – 12.22%, protein (6.56 – 38.83%), fat (1.45- 20.16%),
Ash (1.57-3.03%), fiber (2.00-3.55%) and carbohydrate (25.95-82.56%). Lactobacillaceae
significantly (p < 0.05) improved the nutritional indices of the sourdough bread samples with
increase in protein (14.46%), fat (8.96%), fiber (5.03%) and Ash (1.71%) against 8.45, 4.16, 1.88
and 1.07%, respectively, for protein, fat, fiber and ash content recorded for the control (bread
leavened with yeast). The benefits of sourdough-fermented bread on glycemic index showed
estimated glycemic value of 58.04% against 76.93% recorded for control sample. Shelf life
improved to 9 days while control sample remained at 5 days. Sourdough fermentation is a valuable
natural alteration for increasing the quality of bread. Combination of wheat, orange flesh potato
and soybean in sourdough bread production will be of great importance in the preparation of bread
that does not require high gluten and glycemic content.
Keyword: Functional, nutritional, glycemic, sourdough bread, Lactobacillus, yeast

candidates.abstract: Plant polyphenols are ubiquitous secondary metabolites in plants whose antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and cardioprotective activities have been systematically elucidated. They exert their physiological functions by scavenging intracellular reactive oxygen species, precisely regulating inflammatory mediators, and inhibiting pathogenic proliferation, exhibiting tremendous application potential in functional foods, biomedicine, and natural cosmetics. However, the inherent chemical instability of polyphenols leads to severe structural degradation and bioactivity loss during extraction, processing, and storage. This manifests not only as detectable content reduction but also as significant "hidden bioactivity loss" without apparent content changes, which has emerged as the core bottleneck restricting their industrial translation. Most existing reviews are limited to single-stage optimizations, and a systematic regulatory framework spanning the entire process of biosynthesis, extraction, and processing has not yet been established. In this narrative critical review, we construct an integrated system for polyphenol content enhancement and stability regulation across the entire value chain from biosynthesis to extraction and processing. We critically elaborate on stress-mediated biosynthetic mechanisms, extraction loss control strategies, and processing stabilization technologies, with the ultimate goal of improving their resource utilization efficiency and advancing the industrial innovation and application of plant polyphenols.

candidates.abstract:
Abstract
                  Far-red (FR) light can enhance photosynthesis over short timescales, even at irradiances above the light-limited range. However, it remains unclear whether increasing FR beyond the fraction naturally present in direct sunlight further stimulates photosynthesis, and whether changes in mesophyll conductance to CO2 (gm) contribute to this response. Tomato leaves developed under artificial sunlight-mimicking PAR (16 h; 300 μmol PAR m−2 s−1) with a far-red fraction representative of direct sunlight (R:FR ratio 1.1) were exposed to two actinic light regimes (constant and sinusoidal intensity patterns) combined with three R:FR ratios (10.5, 1.1 and 0.48), representing FR fractions below, similar to, and above those occurring in direct sunlight. High-temporal-resolution gas exchange and carbon isotope (δ13C) measurements (0.2 Hz) were used to quantify gm, stomatal conductance (gs), net CO2 assimilation (Anet) and chloroplastic CO2 concentration. Increasing FR from a low level to the fraction occurring in direct sunlight enhanced both gm and Anet throughout the photoperiod in both actinic light regimes. However, a further increase in FR to levels characteristic of foliar shade did not result in additional increases in either gm or Anet. Estimates of chloroplastic CO2 concentration suggest that the FR-induced increase in apparent gm may help sustain chloroplastic CO2 supply as assimilation increases, but is not sufficient to explain the stimulation of Anet. These results indicate that the short-term photosynthetic response to FR is already established at the FR fraction occurring in direct sunlight and does not increase further with additional FR.

candidates.title: Distinct phytochrome-specific regulation of tomato sugar metabolism and plant architecture by far-red light
candidates.abstract:
Abstract
                  Phytochromes are a family of plant photoreceptors specialized in detecting red and far-red light (FR). Increased FR levels can trigger the shade avoidance syndrome, typically leading to morphological adjustments enhancing light perception. FR can also increase plant sugar levels by an unknown mechanism, and the roles of individual phytochromes in these responses remain largely unclear. Here, we used reverse genetics and FR trials in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum cv. Moneymaker) to assess the involvement of five phytochromes in different architectural, physiological, and sugar metabolism-related changes. Although FR had no direct positive effect on leaf photosynthesis, overall plant photosynthetic capacity increased, probably due to FR-induced architectural changes improving light capture. We found that phyB2 was involved in regulating this whole-plant photosynthesis response to FR. Our results using phy mutants indicated that FR can also directly affect tomato sugar metabolism independently of architectural and physiological changes. We found a critical role for phyE in regulating carbohydrate levels. We also found that phyB1 and phyB2 regulate source–sink dynamics under FR, and that phyA is potentially a negative regulator of sink strength under FR. Collectively, our work revealed distinct roles for individual phytochromes in coordinating FR-specific architectural and sugar metabolism responses in tomato.

candidates.title: Red–Blue and White Supplementary Light Increase Carotenoid Accumulation and Improve Fruit Quality in Satsuma Mandarin: Associations with Chlorophyll Content and Carotenogenic Gene Expression
candidates.abstract: Light regulates plant growth and secondary metabolism. To improve the nutritional quality and economic benefits of satsuma mandarin (Citrus unshiu Marc.) under greenhouse conditions with reduced natural light, we investigated the effects of supplementary lighting with different light qualities and intensities on fruit coloration, carotenoid accumulation, and fruit quality. Supplementary lighting was applied from 156 days after flowering using red, blue, red–blue combinations, and white light. All treatments significantly increased the color contribution index and total carotenoid content in both the rind and flesh compared with the control, with the red–blue light RB14 and white light W1 treatments being the most effective. β-Cryptoxanthin, the major carotenoid in satsuma mandarin, increased by 120.3% and 97.6% under RB14 and W1, respectively. Supplementary lighting also significantly increased the soluble sugar, total soluble solid, ascorbic acid, amino acid, flavonoid, and phenolic acid contents at most sampling time points. The leaf chlorophyll content increased, and chlorophyll degradation was delayed. qRT-PCR showed that RB14 and W1 upregulated the key carotenoid biosynthesis genes CitPSY, CitPDS, CitZDS, CitCRTISO, CitLCYE, CitLCYB, CitBCH2, CitZEP, and CitVDE and downregulated CitCCD4. These results suggest that supplementary lighting may enhance carotenoid accumulation and improve fruit quality by increasing the chlorophyll content and modulating carotenogenic gene expression, thereby providing a theoretical basis for citrus quality improvement.

candidates.title: Effects of Red and Blue Light on Steady-State and Dynamic Photosynthesis of Cucumber Seedlings
candidates.abstract: Our previous study revealed a significant effect of red and blue light on steady-state and dynamic photosynthesis in cucumber seedlings. To further investigate the mechanism by which red and blue light affect photosynthesis, cucumber (Cucumis sativus L. cv. Jinyou 365) seedlings were exposed to white light (W), monochromatic red light (R), monochromatic blue light (B), and mixed red–blue light with red:blue photon flux ratios of 9:1 (9R1B), 7:3 (7R3B), 5:5 (5R5B), 3:7 (3R7B), and 1:9 (1R9B). We measured photosynthetic pigment contents, induction curves of photosynthetic gas exchange and chlorophyll fluorescence parameters during low-to-high-light transition, as well as the activities and gene expression of key Calvin cycle enzymes. The results showed that B yielded higher photosynthetic pigment contents than R, although both remained lower than W. Mixed red–blue light with a blue-light ratio above 50% produced significantly higher pigment contents than W. Under low light, blue light exhibited negligible effects on photosynthesis. In contrast, under high light, 7R3B, 5R5B, 3R7B and 1R9B elevated net photosynthetic rate (A) and stomatal conductance (Gs). Among these, 7R3B, 5R5B and 3R7B also accelerated photoinduction, as reflected by a shorter time to reach 90% steady-state net photosynthetic rate (T90%A). Chlorophyll fluorescence parameters changed rapidly and attained a steady state within 5 min during light induction. During photoinduction, biochemical limitation was severe in the early stage but declined rapidly, while stomatal limitation appeared in mid-induction and persisted into the late stage; photochemical limitation remained minor, and the severity of these limitations was modified by light quality. Red and blue light exerted negligible effects on chlorophyll fluorescence parameters under low light. However, blue light enhanced the relative electron transport rate of PSII under high light by elevating the fraction of open PSII centers. Furthermore, blue light significantly increased the activities and gene expression of key Calvin cycle enzymes. Correlation analysis revealed that higher chlorophyll contents were positively associated with A and Gs under high light but showed no significant correlation with photoinduction. Higher A and Gs under both low- and high-light intensities were associated with faster photoinduction.

candidates.abstract: Purple celery (Apium graveolens L.) is a high-value functional vegetable rich in anthocyanins, but achieving a balanced optimization between biomass accumulation and nutritional quality in plant factories remains challenging due to species-specific spectral trade-offs, and current research lacks integrated light recipes that simultaneously optimize photosynthetic efficiency, antioxidant defenses, and functional quality while suppressing nitrate accumulation. This study evaluated five LED treatments over 30 days: white light (CK), monochromatic red (R), and red-to-blue photon flux density ratios of 5:5, 7:3, and 8:2. Red light induced stem elongation but suppressed root development. Conversely, 8R2B delivered the best performance, significantly elevating leaf, petiole, root, and total fresh biomass and increasing total dry weight by 68.8% over CK. It also markedly enhanced chlorophyll a, b, total chlorophyll, and carotenoids, as well as improved PSII quantum yield (YII), photochemical quenching (qP), and electron transport rate (ETR), while reducing non-photochemical heat dissipation (NPQ) by 61.0%, indicating superior light-use efficiency. Furthermore, 8R2B upregulated CAT and POD activities promoted soluble sugars (up 688.4% in leaves), soluble proteins, and ascorbic acid accumulation, yet reduced leaf nitrate by 28.5%. Principal component analysis confirmed 8R2B as the most effective formulation across all growth, photochemical, defense, and quality traits. These findings provide a novel, evidence-based 8:2 red-to-blue LED light recipe for high-yield, high-quality, and commercially viable purple celery production in controlled environment agriculture.

candidates.abstract:
Purpose
                    To address the optimization problem of spatial robotic arm locking-unit layout, this study proposes a collaborative optimization method based on the adaptive growth patterns of plant roots. The approach aims to enhance the fundamental frequency of the robotic arm system while reducing the number of locking units.
                  
                  
                    Design/methodology/approach
                    Drawing upon the adaptive growth principles of monocotyledonous roots, a collaborative optimization model for the position–stiffness–quantity of locking units was established. By constructing simplified spatial robotic arm models and three-dimensional spring-support models, parallel optimization algorithms were used to simulate and optimize the robotic arm’s distributed locking units. The simulation results were compared and verified with the step-by-step optimization approach.
                  
                  
                    Findings
                    The collaborative optimization method significantly enhances the maximum fundamental frequency of the robotic arm while effectively reducing the number of locking units required. Compared to the step-by-step optimization approach, this method demonstrates clear advantages in both dynamic performance and weight reduction.
                  
                  
                    Research limitations/implications
                    This paper does not compare the computational efficiency and accuracy of the collaborative optimization method with those of general optimization algorithms, thereby limiting evaluation of the method’s performance in other aspects.
                  
                  
                    Originality/value
                    By incorporating the adaptive growth pattern of monocotyledonous plant roots into the layout design of space robotic arm locking units, a multi-parameter collaborative optimization model and method for locking-unit position–stiffness–quantity were established. This approach overcomes the limitations of step-by-step optimization methods, offering new insights into the layout design of locking units in complex multi-joint mechanisms such as space robotic arms.

candidates.title: Pathogenic Characteristics and Chemical Control of Soybean Leaf Anthracnose Caused by Colletotrichum sojae Newly Found in Northeast China
candidates.abstract:
Soybean (
                    Glycine max
                    ) leaf anthracnose, caused by diverse pathogenic agents, poses a significant threat to global soybean production. In 2025, a pathogenic fungus was isolated from symptomatic soybean leaves collected in a major soybean-producing region of China. Morphological and molecular characterization confirmed that the isolates belong to
                    Colletotrichum sojae
                    . To our knowledge, this is the first report of
                    C. sojae
                    causing soybean leaf anthracnose in Northeast China. Among the 15
                    C. sojae
                    isolates tested, moderately virulent strains were predominant, accounting for approximately 53.3%. Host range determination demonstrated that
                    C. sojae
                    could infect lentil, tomato, cowpea, peanut, kidney bean, broad bean, mung bean, and corn, but failed to infect red adzuki bean. Fungicide bioassays showed that tebuconazole and difenoconazole exhibited the highest inhibitory efficacy, with each fungicide achieving full mycelial growth inhibition at 0.05 mg·liter
                    −1
                    . Moreover, foliar spraying with tebuconazole at 0.00014 mg·liter
                    −1
                    and difenoconazole at 0.0005 mg·liter
                    −1
                    reduced disease incidence by roughly 76%. Therefore, intercropping of host and nonhost plants, combined with the application of the aforementioned chemical fungicides, can be considered as effective strategies for controlling soybean leaf anthracnose. These results establish a scientific foundation for managing
                    C. sojae
                    -associated soybean leaf anthracnose in Northeast China.

candidates.title: Epidermal Flavonoids as a Potential Target Trait to Breed for Intrinsic Heat Tolerance in Wheat ( Triticum aestivum  L.)
candidates.abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    In crop plants, epidermal flavonoids play a predominant role in photoprotection. To date, however, there has been no attempt to exploit the flavonoids as a biomarker in breeding for heat tolerance because routine phenotyping is neither practicable nor cost‐effective. A portable, non‐destructive fluorescence device, the Dualex Scientific sensor, has been used to estimate total epidermal flavonoids in a wide range of plant species. Our objectives in the current research were to investigate which of the flavonoids in wheat (
                    
                      Triticum aestivum
                    
                    L.) can be predicted from sensor readings obtained using the device, test its potential as a target trait to breed for heat tolerance and investigate the genetics through genome‐wide quantitative trait loci (QTL) and prediction analyses. A targeted analysis of several metabolites found that Flav index from the Dualex sensor was highly correlated with the isoorientin content of the leaf (
                    R
                    2
                     = 0.9) and furthermore, cultivars rated as heat‐tolerant versus sensitive showed significant differences in isoorientin contents when exposed to artificial heat stress in the field. Using the Flav index as a proxy, a genome‐wide QTL analysis identified eight single‐nucleotide polymorphic markers associated with the trait. The individual loci explained between 2% and 30% of the phenotypic variation, and the major‐effect locus mapped close to a wheat ortholog of the maize gene (
                    ZmUGT708A6
                    ), which encodes a
                    C‐glycosyltransferase
                    and requires further validation. We further investigated genomic selection using molecular markers alone and found the prospects to be high, with a prediction accuracy of 0.69 ± 0.003. In conclusion, our results suggest that high concentration of isoorientin in wheat leaves, which could be accurately predicted using fluorescence imaging, are associated with heat tolerance in wheat. Furthermore, the wheat crop could be a valuable source of this health‐promoting compound.

Nano-Biochar Mediated Regulation of Antioxidant Defense System and Oxidative Stress Responses in Maize (Zea mays L.) Under Drought Stress Conditions
candidates.abstract: Drought stress promotes the overproduction of reactive oxygen species (ROS), causing oxidative damage that limits maize growth and productivity. This study evaluated the effects of foliar-applied nano-biochar and sulphur on oxidative stress and antioxidant defense in maize (Zea mays L. cv. FH-1046) under drought. A pot experiment was conducted in a completely randomized design with two moisture regimes (control, 75–80% field capacity; drought, 35–40% field capacity) and three foliar treatments (distilled water, 3% nano-biochar, 12 mg L⁻¹ sulphur), with five replicates. Foliar sprays were applied 50 days after emergence, and leaf biochemical traits were measured 15 days later. Drought increased hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) content by 24% on average (P < 0.001), but the increase was confined to sulphur-treated plants (765.9 vs. 491.3 nmol g⁻¹ FW under well-watered conditions). Sulphur increased superoxide dismutase activity by 32% relative to the water spray, whereas nano-biochar increased peroxidase activity under drought by 83%. Drought induced a 4.6-fold increase in ascorbate peroxidase activity in unsprayed plants, but not in plants sprayed with nano-biochar or sulphur, and both sprays lowered total phenolics, mainly under well-watered conditions. Malondialdehyde, ascorbic acid, soluble sugars and free amino acids were not significantly affected. Neither spray reduced H₂O₂ or malondialdehyde, so these results do not demonstrate improved oxidative status or drought tolerance. The effects of foliar nano-biochar and sulphur on antioxidant responses were trait-specific and depended on water availability, and their consequences for growth and yield require further testing.

candidates.title: IN VITRO GROWTH OF POTATO (SOLANUM TUBEROSUM L.) CULTIVAR GRANOLA PLANTLETS UNDER DROUGHT STRESS INDUCED BY VARIOUS CONCENTRATIONS OF MANNITOL
candidates.abstract: Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) is one of the important food commodities with high economic value in Indonesia, with Granola being the most widely cultivated cultivar. The productivity of this cultivar often decreases due to drought stress. This study aimed to determine the growth response of potato plantlets of the Granola cultivar to various concentrations of mannitol as a simulation of drought stress and to determine the mannitol concentration that can still be tolerated by the plantlets. This study employed a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with one factor, namely the addition of mannitol at concentrations of 0 M, 0.1 M, 0.2 M, 0.3 M, and 0.4 M. Each concentration was replicated five times. The research data consisted of qualitative and quantitative data. Qualitative data were presented using a comparative descriptive approach and supplemented with photographic documentation, while quantitative data were tested for homogeneity of variance using Levene’s test at a 5% significance level. If the data were homogeneous, an analysis of variance (ANOVA) was performed. When significant differences were detected, the analysis was followed by Tukey’s HSD test at the 5% significance level. The results showed that the application of mannitol as a simulation of drought stress induced changes in the morphological and physiological responses of potato plantlets of the Granola cultivar. Increasing mannitol concentrations tended to decrease plantlet height, number of leaves, and number of shoots, accompanied by changes in plantlet appearance from green to greenish-brown and eventually brown, as well as reductions in chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, and total chlorophyll contents. Potato plantlets of the Granola cultivar were still able to maintain growth under 0.1 M and 0.2 M mannitol treatments, whereas increasing the concentration to 0.3 M and 0.4 M resulted in greater growth inhibition.

candidates.title: OsDREB1B regulates cold and salt stress responses in rice (Oryza sativa L.)
Antioxidant Defense, Lignin Biosynthesis and Hormone Signaling Coordinately Mediate the Response of Solanum tuberosum L. to Alkaline Salt Stress
candidates.abstract: Alkaline salt stress is an important abiotic stress factor that restricts the growth and development of potato (Solanum tuberosum L.). It can induce oxidative damage, disrupt cellular structures, and disturb endogenous hormone homeostasis, thereby impairing normal plant growth and development. However, the physiological mechanisms underlying potato responses to alkaline salt stress, as well as the relationships among antioxidant defense, lignin accumulation, and changes in endogenous hormone levels, remain to be fully elucidated. Therefore, a systematic investigation of potato responses to alkaline salt stress at both the physiological and gene expression levels is needed to provide further insights into the underlying stress-response mechanisms. In this study, potato cultivar ‘Atlantic’ was used as the experimental material, and a pot experiment was conducted with four NaHCO3 concentrations: 0 mmol/L (CK), 20 mmol/L (T1), 40 mmol/L (T2), and 60 mmol/L (T3). Changes in the antioxidant system, root lignin accumulation, and endogenous hormone contents under different levels of alkaline salt stress were quantitatively analyzed. In addition, the expression patterns of genes involved in lignin biosynthesis (phenylpropanoid pathway) and ABA, GA, and BR signaling pathways were examined to establish an integrated model of the responses involving antioxidant defense, hormone regulation, and lignin biosynthesis. The results showed that the degree of oxidative stress progressively increased with increasing NaHCO3 concentration. SOD (superoxide dismutase) activity and the contents of MDA (malondialdehyde) and GSH (glutathione) continuously increased, whereas POD(peroxidase) and CAT (catalase) activities exhibited a pattern of first increasing and then decreasing, reaching their maximum levels under 40 mmol/L NaHCO3 treatment. Root lignin content increased progressively with increasing stress intensity. In addition, alkaline salt stress significantly affected endogenous hormone levels, with ABA and BR contents increasing and GA content decreasing as the NaHCO3 concentration increased. Further analysis revealed that alkaline salt stress altered the expression of genes involved in the phenylpropanoid pathway and ABA (abscisic acid), GA (gibberellin), and BR (brassinosteroid) signaling pathways, indicating coordinated responses involving antioxidant defense, lignin biosynthesis, and hormonal regulation. In conclusion, potato responds to alkaline salt stress by enhancing antioxidant defense, promoting lignin accumulation, and modulating endogenous hormone balance, which may contribute to its adaptation to alkaline salt stress. This study provides insights into the regulatory mechanisms underlying potato responses to alkaline salt stress and provides a theoretical basis for stress-resilient potato cultivation and the breeding of salt- and alkali-tolerant cultivars in saline-alkali soils.

candidates.title: On-farm Evaluation of Improved Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) Varieties through Frontline Demonstrations in the Indo-Burma Plains of Manipur, India
candidates.journal: International Journal of Bio-resource and Stress Management
candidates.abstract: The experiment was conducted during December, 2022–23 and 2023–2024 at four different locations to study varietal performance in the Indo-Burma plains of Manipur. Frontline demonstrations (FLD) of four high-yielding potato varieties, Kufri Chipsona-1, Kufri Pukhraj, Kufri Girdhari, and Kufri Kanchan, were conducted in farmers’ fields at four locations, i.e., Haorong Sabal, Kwasiphai, Mayang Langjing, and Phumlou, in the Imphal West district of Manipur. Across the demonstrations, Kufri Girdhari recorded the highest plant height, while Kufri Pukhraj produced the maximum number of stems per plant and the highest tuber weight per hill. Kufri Kanchan showed the highest performance in terms of tubers per hill, number of tubers per m2 and tuber weight per m2. It also recorded the highest total and marketable tuber yields. Kufri Chipsona-1 produced the highest number of small-sized tubers, whereas medium-sized tubers were most abundant in Kufri Pukhraj. Overall, Kufri Kanchan produced the highest total tuber yield, marketable tuber yield, and number of large-sized tubers. From the demonstrations, it was found that potato varieties Kufri Kanchan, Kufri Pukhraj and Kufri Girdhari performed well under the agro–climatic conditions of Imphal West district, Manipur. These varieties were recommended for large-scale production and horizontal area expansion to enhance productivity and improve farmers’ income and livelihood.

candidates.title: Genome-Wide Characterization and Expression Analysis of the nsLTP Gene Family in Potato (Solanum tuberosum) in Response to Drought Stress
candidates.abstract: Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) is the fourth largest food crop in the world, and drought stress seriously affects its yield and quality. Plant non-specific lipid transfer proteins (nsLTPs) play an important role in resisting biotic and abiotic stresses. Although the functions of nsLTPs have been reported in crops such as rice (Oryza sativa L.) and Arabidopsis thaliana, the systematic identification and functional analysis of nsLTPs in potato, a key food crop sensitive to drought, remain very scarce. In this study, the whole genome identification, drought stress expression analysis and potential function prediction of the potato StnsLTP gene family were carried out by bioinformatics and real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). A total of 123 potato StnsLTP genes were identified, which were unevenly distributed on 11 chromosomes. The encoded amino acid length was 88–390 aa, and 91.1% of StnsLTP proteins were hydrophobic. Conserved motif analysis showed that motif 4 was the most important conserved motif in this family. There were 0–4 introns and 1–4 exons. The family identified 45 pairs of tandem duplicated genes and 20 pairs of segmentally duplicated genes, and the nsLTP potato genes showed close phylogenetic relationships with tomato nsLTP genes. Combined with transcriptome data, three PEG-responsive candidate genes, StnsLTP.115, StnsLTP.117, and StnsLTP.118, were screened. After polyethylene glycol 6000 (PEG 6000) simulated drought treatment, the three genes showed different degrees of induced expression in the roots, stems and leaves of the three potato cultivars, and their expression differed markedly across cultivars, tissues and sampling time points. This study systematically elucidated the structure and evolutionary characteristics of the potato StnsLTP family, and identified three candidate genes responsive to PEG-simulated drought stress. This not only provides a basic reference for the functional study of the potato StnsLTP family, but also offers clues for analyzing potato drought response pathways and exploring candidate genes for potato stress response research.

candidates.title: The potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) transcription factor StPHR1 responds to low phosphate stress and regulates phosphorus accumulation
candidates.abstract:
Phosphorus is an essential macronutrient for plant growth and development. Potato is highly sensitive to inorganic phosphate (Pi) availability, yet the function and regulation of StPHR1, a putative core component of plant Pi signaling, remain poorly defined in this crop. Evolutionary analysis, subcellular localization assays, promoter activity analysis, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing, overexpression, and data-independent acquisition proteomics were used to characterize StPHR1.
                    StPHR1
                    encoded a nuclear-localized MYB-CC transcription factor, whose promoter exhibits preferential activity in root tips and vascular tissues. Loss of
                    StPHR1
                    function compromised low-Pi tolerance, reduced Pi accumulation in roots and leaves, and inhibited plant growth, whereas
                    StPHR1 overexpression enhanced
                    low-Pi tolerance and increased both tuber number and average tuber weight under conventional fertilized cultivation. Proteomic profiling showed that StPHR1-dependent Pi starvation responses involve metabolic reprogramming, membrane-lipid remodeling, redox homeostasis, and detoxification. These results identify
                    StPHR1
                    as a key regulator of Pi accumulation and allocation in potato and provide candidate targets and a molecular framework for improving low-Pi adaptation.

IbMYB11 Involved in Drought Stress Responses Through Association with Flavonoid Metabolism in Sweet Potato
candidates.abstract: Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas (L.) Lam.) is a high-yielding crop that serves as both a food source and a raw material for industrial processing. Drought stress severely impairs sweet potato yield and quality. A MYB-type transcription factor, IbMYB11, was previously identified as a differentially expressed gene induced by drought stress from our previous comparative transcriptome analysis. In this study, we characterized its potential roles in drought tolerance and flavonoid metabolism in sweet potato. Subcellular localization analysis revealed that IbMYB11 localizes to the nucleus. Overexpression of IbMYB11 enhanced SOD and POD activities in transgenic sweet potato plants under drought stress, whereas these activities were significantly reduced in IbMYB11-RNAi plants, suggesting that IbMYB11 may confer drought tolerance by improving the capacity to scavenge reactive oxygen species. Transcriptome and metabolome analyses of IbMYB11-OE, IbMYB11-RNAi, and wild-type plants under simulated drought stress further revealed that the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from all comparison groups were enriched in the flavonoid biosynthesis pathway, and nine flavonoid metabolites were identified among the differentially accumulated metabolites. Furthermore, differentially expressed TFs and flavonoid metabolites were jointly subjected to WGCNA, yielding 12 hub genes and modules significantly associated with flavonoid metabolites. Collectively, this study demonstrates that IbMYB11 improved drought tolerance, likely in part via its association with flavonoid metabolism, and providing valuable genetic resources for molecular design breeding of drought-resistant sweet potato.

candidates.abstract: Heat shock protein 40 (DnaJ/HSP40) co-chaperones are key regulators of protein folding, cellular homeostasis, and stress adaptation in plants. Although individual HSP40 proteins have been functionally characterized in tomato and HSP40 members have also been examined within broader HSP chaperone networks, an integrated characterization of the tomato HSP40 family combining evolutionary relationships, structural features, promoter regulation, tissue-specific expression, multi-stress transcriptomic profiling, and experimental expression validation remains limited. In this study, a systematic genome-wide analysis identified 95 tomato HSP40 genes, which were classified into three phylogenetic groups. The encoded proteins contained conserved J-domains, and distinct conserved motif distributions, while the genes exhibited variable exon–intron organization. Chromosomal mapping revealed an uneven distribution across the 12 tomato chromosomes, with segmental duplication representing the predominant duplication pattern contributing to HSP40 family expansion. Promoter analysis identified 37 distinct types of cis-regulatory elements associated with hormone signaling, growth and development, and abiotic stress responses, indicating complex transcriptional regulation. Tissue-specific expression analysis showed that the majority of HSP40 genes were expressed across multiple tissues and developmental stages, whereas several members exhibited preferential or limited expression patterns. Transcriptomic profiling under drought, salinity, and heat stress revealed dynamic and stress-dependent regulation, with some genes showing consistent induction across multiple stresses and others being markedly repressed. qRT-PCR analysis of selected HSP40 genes further confirmed distinct temporal responses to drought, salinity, and heat stress, supporting their potential involvement in abiotic stress adaptation. Collectively, these findings provide an integrated genomic, evolutionary, structural, and transcriptional framework for the tomato HSP40 family and identify candidate genes for future functional validation and molecular breeding strategies aimed at improving tomato resilience to abiotic stress.

Effects of Bay Leaf (Laurus nobilis L.), Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) Peel and Banana (Musa Species) Peel Extracts on Bio-Chemical Indicators of Some Upland Rice (Oryza sativa L.) Crop under Higher Iron in Acid Soil Condition

candidates.abstract: Background: The occurrence of high rainfall in Assam and leaching of base cations cause the soils to become acidic in reaction. The high mobility of iron in acid soil and its absorption raises the iron concentration, and it damages the physiology of crop plants. That is why excessive iron is regarded as one of the limiting factors responsible for lowering growth, development and yield of upland rice crop under irrigation through shallow tube wells. An innovative approach using extracts of potassium- and antioxidant-rich bio-inputs might be a novel approach for deterring and halting physio-biochemical aberrations due to higher iron in acid soil condition. Method: A pot experiment (CRBD with three replications) was carried out to investigate the effects of bay leaf, potato peel, and banana peel extracts on biochemical indicators of some upland (Ahu) rice crop (varieties: Inglongkiri, Dehangi (Fe tolerant), Lachit (Fe susceptible), and Luit) under higher iron in acid soil conditions during the Autumn season (March-September, 2024). The five treatments were: (1) 100 ppm FeSO₄ as basal at vegetative stage (control), (2) 100 ppm FeSO₄ as basal at vegetative stage plus root dip treatment before transplanting and foliar spray with bay leaf extract at 20 days after transplanting, (3) 100 ppm FeSO₄ as basal at vegetative stage plus root dip treatment before transplanting and foliar spray with banana peel extract at 20 days after transplanting, (4) 100 ppm FeSO₄ as basal at vegetative stage plus root dip treatment before transplanting and foliar spray with potato peel extract at 20 days after transplanting; (5) Natural soil without any treatment (absolute control). Result: In general, compared to the control, the treatments significantly increased biochemical indices viz., total chlorophyll (10.80-21.90%), chlorophyll 'a' (6.39-20.93%), chlorophyll 'b' contents (7.27-22.35%) at maximum tillering stage; total chlorophyll (10.96-21.38%), chlorophyll 'a' (11.88-21.89%), chlorophyll 'b' contents at heading stage (7.22-15.79%), NR activity at maximum tillering (12.43-35.52%) and heading (15-36.23%) stages, carbohydrate content (7.51-13.81%) and reduced iron content (10.57-21.34%) in grain at harvest. The bio-input extracts lessened cation leakage at maximum tillering (2.25-1.63%) and heading (3.52-2.83%) stages, and lipid peroxidation at maximum tillering (30.03-10.55%) and heading (29.64-10.96%) stages, despite the presence of high iron in the soil (initial: 200 ppm, harvest: 106 ppm). In the experiment, the intensity of blue colour following Perl's Prussian Blue staining was directly related to iron content in grain, with darker staining indicating higher iron accumulation, and this was altered by the bio-input treatments.

candidates.title: Interactive Effects of Salicylic Acid and Sowing Dates on Growth and Yield Attributes of Potato (<i>Solanum tuberosum</i> L.)
candidates.abstract: Optimizing sowing time and exogenous application of salicylic acid (SA) is essential for enhancing growth, tuberization, and yield of potato under abiotic stress conditions, particularly low temperature. A field experiment was conducted during the 2024–2025 growing season to evaluate the interactive effects of different sowing dates and foliar-applied salicylic acid on vegetative growth, tuber size distribution, yield, and plant survival of potato (Solanum tuberosum L.). The experiment consisted of three sowing dates (October 01, October 15, and October 29) and four SA concentrations (0, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 mM), arranged in a factorial design. Analysis of variance revealed that sowing dates (SD), salicylic acid levels (SA), and their interaction (SD × SA) had significant effects on all measured parameters. Early sowing on October 01 resulted in significantly higher plant height (50.1 cm), greater leaf number (35 plant⁻¹), increased number of large tubers (2.7 plant⁻¹), maximum total tuber yield (22.0 t ha⁻¹), and highest plant survival (94%). In contrast, delayed sowing on October 29 led to reduced growth, lower yield, decreased survival, and increased production of small-sized tubers. Foliar application of salicylic acid significantly enhanced growth and yield attributes up to an optimum concentration of 1.5 mM. Application at this level increased leaf number, reduced the number of small tubers, improved large tuber formation, enhanced total tuber yield (20.1 t ha⁻¹), and increased plant survival (83%). However, a higher concentration (2.0 mM) exhibited inhibitory effects on several growth and yield traits. The interaction between sowing date and salicylic acid demonstrated that early sowing (October 01) combined with 1.5 mM SA consistently produced superior results across all growth, yield, and survival parameters. These findings suggest that early October sowing coupled with foliar application of salicylic acid at 1.5 mM is an effective agronomic strategy for improving potato productivity and stand establishment under similar agro-ecological conditions.

candidates.title: Transcriptome and Hormone Analysis Revealed Jasmonic Acid-Mediated Immune Responses of Potato (Solanum tuberosum) to Potato Spindle Tuber Viroid Infection
candidates.abstract: Potato is a globally important non-cereal crop in which infection with potato spindle tuber viroid (PSTVd) can cause stunted growth and significantly reduce tuber yield. We previously showed that PSTVd induces accumulation of the plant hormone jasmonic acid (JA) and alters antioxidant responses in potato plants. To clarify the role of JA in response to PSTVd, we analyzed disease development in transgenic JA-deficient opr3 and JA-insensitive coi1 lines compared to the wild-type. Transcriptomic analysis using RNA-Seq revealed that most genotype-specific differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in all comparisons were enriched in plant hormone signal transduction, plant-pathogen interaction, and MAPK signaling pathways, although the number of DEGs varied. These differences were confirmed by independent data from RT-qPCR, hormone, and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) analyses. After PSTVd infection, opr3 plants showed enhanced JA signaling and increased abscisic acid (ABA) and auxin (AUX) content. In contrast, coi1 plants showed reduced ABA, AUX, and salicylic acid content. Both opr3 and coi1 plants showed reduced JA and H2O2 content and lower expression of defense-related genes, resulting in milder symptoms but increased viroid accumulation. In addition, treatment with methyl jasmonate alleviated symptoms in infected wild-type plants. Together, these results indicate a modulatory role for JA and JA signaling in basal immune responses and symptom development in the potato-PSTVd interaction.

candidates.title: Effect of sucrose and abscisic acid on potato (Solanum tuberosum) microtuberisation and dormancy
candidates.journal: The Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences
candidates.abstract: Microtuberisation serves as a vital approach for the rapid propagation and long-term conservation of potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) germplasm. The present study was carried out during 2023–24 at Sardarkrushinagar Dantiwada Agriculture University, Dantiwada, Gujarat to evaluate the interactive effects of abscisic acid (ABA), sucrose concentrations, and genotype on in vitro microtuber formation across four potato cultivars, i.e. Kufri Badshah, Kufri Surya, Lady Rosetta, and Kufri Nilkanth. Nodal explants were cultured in Murashige and Skoog (MS) liquid medium supplemented with ABA (0.0, 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 mg/L) and sucrose (8% and 10%) to assess their impact on key microtuberisation parameters. Results demonstrated that increased sucrose concentration significantly enhanced higher number of microtubers and microtuber weight, outperforming all treatments involving ABA. The combination of ABA with sucrose did not yield synergistic effects, indicating sucrose as the principal driver of microtuber development. Among the genotype, Kufri Badshah exhibited the highest microtuberisation efficiency, followed by Kufri Surya, Lady Rosetta, and Kufri Nilkanth. While ABA did not directly improve microtuber induction or growth metrics, it played a critical role in dormancy extension and prolongation of storage viability, an essential factor for transportation and germplasm preservation.
